A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProMAG research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite the revised title and reorganized presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments, text-to-video evaluations, efficiency measurements, and component comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds tokenizer comparisons and training/inference cost measurements.

M1.justification: The progressive 4×→8×→16× procedure, frozen pretrained blocks, AdaNorm residual fusion, losses, spatial tiling, and overlapping-frame reconstruction are retained. The architecture specifications match between v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 9; the added discriminator explanation does not introduce a different component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same internal training datasets, MCL-JCV and DAVIS reconstruction benchmarks, VBench evaluation, and long-video generation setting. v2 still describes 360×640 evaluation; omission of its scores changes reported evidence without establishing removal of that scenario.

E2.justification: v2 removes the evaluated OS-VAE, OSP-VAE, and CMD comparators and adds OmniTokenizer, VidTok, Cosmos-CV, CogVideoX, WF-VAE, Wan, Hunyuan, and CV-VAE. Cosmos-CV also joins the 8× reconstruction comparison. MagViT-v2, naive progressive training, and EMA-VFI comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 restricts external-tokenizer comparisons to 8/16 latent channels and adds timing protocols using H100 at 256×256 and A100 at 512×512, with 17-frame inputs. Existing reconstruction and VBench protocols largely persist. Table 3 labels retained 8× GAN-ablation values as eight-channel results, conflicting with their sixteen-channel labeling elsewhere; an actual setting change is not established.

E4.justification: New Appendices E–F analyze training savings and the parameter-count and encoding/decoding costs accompanying reconstruction gains. Existing residual/AdaNorm, external-interpolation, normalization, and tiling analyses remain. The separately presented GAN ablation reuses results already included in v1 Table 1.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five generation seeds per VBench prompt. Neither adds repeated-training statistics, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive baseline and resource results while removing OS-VAE/OSP-VAE/CMD rows and all reported 360×640 reconstruction scores. For example, Table 2 adds Cosmos-CV rFVD 101.36 against retained ProMAG 63.64 on MCL-JCV at 512×512, 8× compression and sixteen channels. Retained ProMAG/MagViT-v2 reconstruction values, component-comparison values, and the VBench plot are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations (1)–(4) are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit approximately 2.7× tokenizer-training speedup claim to the introduction's contributions. The central claims about fixed-channel temporal compression, reconstruction quality, and suitability for efficient DiT generation remain.

C2.justification: v2 explains encoding overhead through two encoder passes, discusses the GAN loss's perceptual-quality/PSNR tradeoff, and clarifies that the fastest tokenizer is not its goal. It removes v1's slower-DiT-convergence limitation and larger-batch explanation for VBench differences. High-motion and chunk-boundary limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents matched baseline iteration budgets, tokenizer timing hardware/workloads, and encoder/decoder parameter counts. It removes the CMD implementation appendix. Core architecture and training hyperparameters, the DiT implementation details, and the project URL remain unchanged; additional budget disclosure does not establish rerunning existing experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds recent tokenizer literature, removes the PVDM/CMD/LaMD discussion, and relates naive progressive training to Open-SORA and OpenSORA-Plan. It sharpens the distinction from MovieGen and Cosmos while retaining the MagViT-v2 foundation, ProGAN inspiration, and principal novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Highly Compressed' to 'Temporally Compact' latent spaces, author ordering changes, and several captions and explanatory passages are edited. Baseline discussion and appendix organization are revised, but the main section sequence and most methodological prose remain.

P2.justification: The large reconstruction table is reorganized into separate base-compression, high-compression, and GAN-ablation tables, and three resource tables are added. Figure 8 becomes a narrower display with fewer frames, and appendix diagrams are relocated and reordered. These substantially change the presentation of evidence, although the underlying method diagrams remain.

improvement.justification: The broader, more relevant tokenizer comparisons and explicit cost/capacity accounting make the unchanged method better supported and easier to assess. Gains are limited by removal of the 360×640 scores and DiT convergence caveat, plus new inconsistencies: Appendix E's per-iteration timings disagree with Table 6, and Table 3 misaligns channel labeling with retained results. These shortcomings prevent a substantial overall improvement.
